To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the naturalness of sonic feedback affects the perceived usability and pleasure of the interface, but the effects of naturalness depend on the type of relationship between the user and the feedback.

naturalness of a sound is a property of the relationship between the sound and the action that produces it, and that the naturalness of the sound is the main factor influencing the perceived usability of the sounds used as interface feedback.

(1) the relationship between the gesture and the feedback influences how natural the sound is perceived, (2) the relationship between gesture and feedback influences the usability and the pleasantness of the sound, and (3) the relationship between sound and interface influences the usability and pleasantness judgments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of naturalness as a key factor in the evaluation of a sound’s usability and pleasantness.
the relationship between the naturalness of the sounds and the perceived usability and pleasure of the human-computer interaction.
the influence of the perceived naturalness of a sound on the perceived pleasantness and usability of the sound.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the causal relationship results in sounds perceived as the most natural, and therefore the most pleasant, and the arbitrary relationship results in sounds that are not perceived as natural, but that are not perceived to be unpleasant either.
naturalness is a key factor in determining the perceived usability and the pleasantness of the feedback sounds.
naturalness influences the perceived pleasantness of an audio feedback and that the perceived naturalness is influenced by the perceived pleasantness.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the naturalness and usability of a human-computer interaction are related, and that the relationship between the user and the interface can be used to manipulate the naturalness of the interaction.
the causal relationship is a key factor in the perception of a sonic feedback as natural.
the relationship between the user and the feedback sound has to be natural for the sound to be perceived as useful and pleasant.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for a given interface, it is possible to design the sounds in a way that makes them more or less usable and more or less pleasant.
the naturalness of the sounds influences the perceived usability of the interface.
naturalness is not only a perceptual quality but also an important factor for the perceived pleasantness and usability of the feedback sounds.
